ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.641 adds GLM-5.1, Escape interrupt, steps 200
ai.summary: Version 1.0.641 ships GLM-5.1 (`z-ai/glm-5.1`) as the default model for `base2-free`, `editor-lite`, and `code-reviewer-lite`, replacing Minimax-M2.5, with new Fireworks pricing and deployment mappings. The update raises MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT from 100 to 200 in common/src/constants/agents.ts, disables the Minimax-M2.5 custom Fireworks deployment mapping, and switches the context-pruner agent model to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6. Additional CLI fixes let Escape on the askuser form properly interrupt the assistant stream by wiring onInterruptStream to ChatInputBar in cli/src/chat.tsx, and token-counting now includes tools converted to Anthropic format for accurate input billing.
ai.evidence: Version field in `cli/release/package.json` incremented from 1.0.640 to 1.0.641; release updates since 1.0.640 include GLM-5.1 replacing Minimax-M2.5 in base2-free/editor-lite/code-reviewer-lite, MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT raised to 200, Minimax-M2.5 deployment disabled in web routing, Escape-on-askuser stream interrupt fixes, Fireworkstest fixture updates, context-pruner agent model switch to claude-sonnet-4.6, and tool inclusion in Anthropic token-counting API.

eli5.text: This release upgrades your CLI with the new GLM-5.1 AI model, which now powers several of the built-in assistants for coding, editing, and reviewing code. It also doubles the maximum number of steps an agent can take in a single run from 100 to 200, giving your automated coding sessions much more room to work through complex tasks. When you are prompted by the assistant and press Escape, the stream is now properly interrupted right away so it stops mid-response instead of finishing. Token usage is now counted more accurately when tools are involved, especially for Anthropic models, helping you avoid overcharged or undercounted credits. Additionally, the assistant that condenses long conversations switched to Claude Sonnet 4.6 for better summarization. Upgrading gives you a smarter, more responsive coding assistant with better cost tracking and fewer stalls on bigger jobs.

ai.title: Freebuff version bumped to 0.0.33
ai.summary: The Freebuff package version has been incremented to 0.0.33, as recorded in cli/release/package.json. This routine release bump follows the prior CLI version bump to 1.0.641 and precedes the next commit adding Minimax M2.7 model support. As a version-only change with no functional code modifications, this release serves as a packaging milestone for the accumulation of recent changes including the context-pruner model switch to claude-sonnet-4.6, tool-aware token counting, and Fireworks routing test fixture updates.
ai.evidence: Commit a2f77e52 bumps the version field in freebuff/cli/release/package.json from 0.0.32 to 0.0.33 (single-line diff, +1/-1 stats). This is a release-bump commit in the packaging category with no other file modifications.

eli5.text: Version 0.0.33 brings smoother and more reliable interactions between you and the AI assistant. When you interrupt an ongoing conversation by pressing Escape on a form asking for your input, the AI now properly stops responding instead of continuing, so you won't get confused by overlapping answers. The tool that condenses long conversations to keep things tidy now runs on a newer, smarter AI model called Claude Sonnet 4.6, which should produce better summaries of your chat history. The system that counts how many words or tokens you use for billing now also accounts for the extra tools and functions available, so your usage tracking stays accurate, especially when using Anthropic-based models. Upgrading gives you a more predictable chat experience when interrupting conversations, improved conversation summaries, and more accurate tracking of your usage.

ai.title: Add minimax m2.7 model support
ai.summary: Added 'minimax/minimax-m2.7' to ModelName union in agent-definition.ts files. Web layer maps this ID to Fireworks standard API model 'accounts/fireworks/models/minimax-m2p7' with pricing set at $0.30/$0.06/$1.20 per million tokens for input/cached/input/output. Scope covers core type definitions, initial agents template, and web fireworks.ts.

eli5.text: Agents can now use a new model called Minimax M2.7, which is the latest version replacing the older M2.5 model. If you looked at the system settings, you'd see pricing details showing that using this model costs money: 30 cents per million input tokens, 6 cents for cached inputs, and 1.20 for every million output tokens. The assistant now recognizes M2.7 as a valid choice and can route calls to the correct backend automatically.

ai.title: Add e2e test for context pruning threshold accuracy
ai.summary: New e2e test agents/e2e/context-pruning-threshold.e2e.test.ts validates context pruning triggers at correct token limits. Addresses previous bug where local overcounting or 30% buffer caused premature pruning at ~140k instead of 200k. Covers Anthropic models via real API token counting, verifies tool-call/result pair integrity post-pruning, and checks for <conversation_summary> or trimMessagesToFitTokenLimit fallback.

eli5.text: If you use Claude's long conversations, the assistant used to start forgetting earlier parts of your chat sooner than it should have, around 140,000 characters instead of the full 200,000 it promises. A new automated check now confirms that trimming only kicks in once you truly hit the limit, so your chat stays complete until then. This is already live and protects everyone who relies on long conversations today.

ai.title: Increase buffbench eval concurrency
ai.summary: Doubles `taskConcurrency` for `runBuffBench` in eval scripts. Nightly runs `base2-free` at 6 (was 3); standard runs `base2-free-evals` at 10 (was 5). Affects `evals/buffbench/main-nightly.ts` and `evals/buffbench/main.ts` only.

eli5.text: The system now runs more of its nightly evaluation tests at the same time, so the backlog of checks finishes sooner behind the scenes. If you monitor internal dashboards, the automated testing runs will show a higher number of tasks completing in parallel, which is why those scheduled checks wrap up faster each day.

ai.title: Minimax M2.7 replaces M2.5 in free agent models
ai.summary: Minimax M2.7 replaces M2.5 across Librarian, Tmux CLI, and free-mode agent sets (base2-free, editor-lite, code-reviewer-lite). Upstream upgrade to m2.7. Scope: agents/librarian/librarian.ts, agents/tmux-cli.ts, common/src/constants/free-agents.ts. isFreeModeAllowedAgentModel prefix check now matches m2.7 dated variants.

eli5.text: When you chat with the Librarian agent that clones and explains a GitHub repo, or with the Tmux CLI agent, and with the free-tier editor/reviewer assistants, the system is now swapping in a newer model called Minimax M2.7 instead of M2.5. You won't notice a flashy difference, but the agents you interact with in free mode (the base orchestrator, the lite editor, and the lite code reviewer) are now pulling answers from this updated model, so responses may read a bit more smoothly or accurately. The change is live today for anyone using those free-mode agents.
